content.thinking:
I'm planning the elephant's proportions and coordinate layout, setting shoulder height around 3.2m with the body spanning roughly -1.5 to 1.3 on the z-axis for rump to chest.

Now I'm designing the skeleton hierarchy: a hips root joint, a spine chain curving up through the back to the chest, then a neck/head joint, followed by a trunk chain that curves down from the head to the ground. I'm working out how to build the body mesh by sweeping a radius function along the spine chain, making sure the hips joint is established as the single root with the spine chain properly parented to it.

Still defining leg geometry...

I need to adjust the leg end target to y=0.32 so the rounded cap dome just barely clears the floor, then layer a sunken foot disc cylinder beneath at y=0.06, plus small toenail boxes near the front of each foot.

Now I'm setting up the leg's IK target: hip at y 1.9 down to the ankle at 0.32 gives a vertical span of 1.58, which is less than the combined bone lengths of 1.7, so the leg bends forward slightly as expected. For the head I'm building a short two-point neck chain rising from the spine's tip joint toward the head position, naming the joints and parenting the chain correctly.

I'm shaping the head with a scaled sphere acting as the skull, a smaller box wedge for the jaw, and a separate trunk chain curling from the base of the face through several forward-dipping points to give it a drooping, curled shape.

Building the trunk chain with catmull curves...

For the tip, I'm adding small dark nostril discs and a dark sphere cap. Now for the ears, I'm planning large Africa-shaped outlines positioned on either side of the head, extruded outward from the face.

Defining the ear outline points...

Now shaping the tusks with a curved bezier sweep from base to tip, using an ivory bone material with a darker base sleeve, then starting on the eye placement with small spheres.

Working out the muzzle taper from forehead to trunk with scaled spheres for cheeks, then placing the jaw joint and box geometry with a mounted bone. For the tail, I'm chaining three points from the rump downward to form tail1, tail2, and tailTip segments.

Now I'm designing the tail tuft with spiky dark cards looping around the tip, then moving to the body coat paint logic, using a mottled countershade with a lighter belly and a cell-based crease function to darken wrinkle lines where cell distances are close together.

I'm adding a dust effect at the feet, mixing toward a reddish-brown dust color as a nod to how real African elephants pick up mud and dust near the ground. For the low-poly look, I'm setting faceted shading on the body sweeps with around 9 sides instead of smooth circles.

Now I'm detailing smaller features: flat-shaded toenails as cones, tusks, a mouth shape, and a few small dark spikes across the crown to suggest sparse hair bristles instead of using card geometry. I'm planning to handle knee wrinkles through paint rather than actual geometry, and I'm adding flattened haunch spheres near the hips to build out the rump shape.

I'm also sketching the body's overall proportions and spine radius profile — checking leg joint heights against the torso, then working out the taper function along the spine chain so the chest dome and rear cap land at reasonable positions, adjusting the hip start point so the rear cap doesn't extend too far back.

I'm trimming the overall body length to fit a more realistic elephant proportion, repositioning the spine's z-range and neck/head placement, then setting shoulder and leg z-coordinates before locking in the actual spine joint coordinates for the chain.

Now I'm defining the neck as a short two-point segment with a constant elliptical sweep radius, capping it near the head so the head sphere sits at the end with slightly flattened width, and linking the head joint's parent back to the neck chain's final joint.

From there I work out the eye positions by projecting onto the head sphere's surface at a given z-offset, placing eyes and brows symmetrically with small sunk radii, then anchor the ears higher up with their own outline widths and flare, and finally set the trunk root position near the face for the next sphere segment.

Working out the trunk path now, curving it forward and down with tapering radius toward a rounded tip, plus small finger-like cones added at the very end.

Then I'm placing a dark sphere for the nostril near the trunk tip, and setting up tusk base positions on either side of the head, curving them outward and up with a catmull path.

Still writing tusk curve points... with ivory coloring and a darker base band. For the tail, I'm chaining tail1, tail2, and tailTip joints from the rump down and back, sweeping the radius from thick to thin, then adding tuft spikes at the end.

Now I'm placing toenail cones on each foot, positioning four per front foot and adjusting for hind feet, tilting the cone axis forward relative to the ankle bone.

For the legs, I'm setting up radius tapering along the limb chain, with hind legs slightly thicker than front, root and target positions keyed off the side offset, and tuning the bend direction so hind legs angle forward and front legs angle back slightly at the elbow.

I'm mapping parent joints from spine to the leg chains, determining left/right naming based on the x-offset sign, and finalizing a palette of about twelve colors covering fur grey tones, belly, dust accents, ivory, nails, dark shading, eyes, mouth, and ear interior.

For the ear coloring, I'm blending between an outer grey and inner pinkish tone based on distance from the attachment point plus a crease effect, deciding to skip normal-based front/back shading for simplicity.

For the mouth I'm placing a small lower lip box on the jaw bone using the skin color, then moving to the forehead where I add two small bump spheres near the top of the head to round out the silhouette, checking the height against the shoulder and ear proportions. For hair, I'm planning crown spikes as thin dark spike shapes positioned around the head top attached to the head bone, while considering whether to add bristly hair along the spine as well.

Now I'm working through the body mesh construction, making sure each bone sweep uses its own joint chain and fixing the radius function's type signature to return a proper tuple instead of a generic array. I'm also pruning unused imports, keeping only the modules I actually use like paint, noise, cells, mix, and smoothstep while dropping things like frame and glow that aren't needed.

For the skin and trunk shading, I'm writing a paint function that samples the base skin color and blends it with a deeper tone wherever a sine-based ring pattern crosses a smoothed threshold, giving the trunk a banded, organic texture.

Now I'm starting to build the actual elephant model, defining the hip joint position and then constructing the spine chain from a catmull curve with named segments, before setting up a sweep function that varies the body's cross-sectional width along the spine using a sine profile.

Next I'm adding the neck as a two-point chain connected to the spine's tip, with its own sweep radius, followed by a head joint attached to the neck's end. I'm assigning roles like "neck," "head," "jaw," "leg," "tail," and treating the trunk as a tentacle-type appendage for the rig structure.

Then I'm attaching the trunk and muzzle geometry to the head bone, painting flattened spheres with proper UVs for facial features, and placing the eyes as dark spheres with amber pupils offset slightly outward. Finally I'm generating a radial loop of tail-tuft spikes positioned around the tail tip using trigonometric offsets for a natural spread.

Now I'm building the foot discs as short cylinders attached to the final leg joint, positioned so they sit flush with the floor, which should complete the model.
